proposed.title: Ontological vs. Epistemic Infinity
proposed.text: This paper distinguishes two senses of 'infinity.' Ontologically, the Library may be infinite in cardinality: it contains all configurations that can be described. Epistemically, however, only coherence-distinguishable equivalence classes matter. Two configurations are coherence-equivalent if no observer-relative coherence condition can distinguish them. The equivalence class is treated as one thing. Thus the 'infinity' of indistinguishable copies collapses to 1 (or 0 for the XOR fixed point). This is not a denial of infinity; it is a structural reduction of multiplicity without ontological reduction.
proposed.latex: x \sim_C y \iff \forall O \in \mathrm{Obs}, \forall h \in H_O, \forall x_0 \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{admissible}}, \delta_O(x,y) = 0
proposed.interpretation: Indistinguishable multiplicity is structurally irrelevant. The Library may be infinite, but the observer only encounters coherence-distinguishable equivalence classes.

_revisions.rationale: Establishes the ontological vs. epistemic distinction upfront, preventing confusion later.

proposed.title: Definition 2.2.1 — Coherence Equivalence
proposed.text: Define an equivalence relation ∼_C on the Library 𝓜. Two configurations x,y ∈ 𝓜 are coherence-equivalent if no observer-relative coherence condition can distinguish them:
proposed.latex: x \sim_C y \iff \forall O \in \mathrm{Obs}, \forall h \in H_O, \forall x_0 \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{admissible}}, \delta_O(x,y) = 0
proposed.interpretation: The equivalence relation identifies configurations that are indistinguishable under all possible observer-relative coherence conditions. This collapses infinite multiplicity into finite equivalence classes for any observer.

_revisions.rationale: Formally introduces the coherence quotient, which is essential for understanding how infinities collapse.

proposed.title: Definition 3.0.1 — Singularity as Coherence Collapse
proposed.text: A singularity in NSFG is a region where the observer-relative coherence quotient 𝓜_C^O collapses to a lower-dimensional or disconnected structure. The singularity is not a property of 𝓜 itself; it is a property of the quotient 𝓜_C^O induced by the observer's coherence condition.
proposed.interpretation: The singularity is where the coherence quotient loses distinguishability, connectivity, or resolution. The Library itself remains unchanged.

_revisions.rationale: Explicitly ties singularities to the coherence quotient, not to the Library directly.
references: Conversation with Uncle (2026-09-02) — Section 5: Impact on Singularity Taxonomy

_revisions.current: The XOR Fixed Point is the unique termination class where distinction collapses.
_revisions.proposed: The XOR Fixed Point is the unique equivalence class in the coherence quotient where all distinction collapses to the identity element 0. In the full Library 𝓜, there may be infinitely many configurations that self-cancel to 0, but in the coherence quotient 𝓜_C, they form a single equivalence class 𝒵 = {0}. Thus the infinity collapses to 1 (the single equivalence class) and ultimately to 0 (the identity element).
_revisions.rationale: Clarifies that the XOR Fixed Point is an equivalence class in the coherence quotient, not a single configuration in the Library.

_revisions.current: A Convergence Boundary is a region where ∀γ1,γ2 ∈ Γ_O(h,x), γ1(n) ∼ γ2(n).

_revisions.rationale: Explicitly ties Convergence Boundaries to the coherence quotient, clarifying that infinite path multiplicity collapses to a single equivalence class.

_revisions.current: The model predicts constant computational cost per tick.
_revisions.proposed: The model predicts constant computational cost per tick because the observer only tracks coherence-distinguishable equivalence classes in 𝓜_C^O, not individual configurations in 𝓜. Formally: Cost per tick = O(|𝓜_C^O(h,x)|) = O(1), where |𝓜_C^O(h,x)| is the number of coherence-distinguishable classes accessible to observer O from history h and reference x. This follows from the static, non-generative structure of the Library and the coherence quotient construction.
_revisions.rationale: Explicitly derives the O(1) core from the coherence quotient, addressing the previous under-derivation concern.

proposed.title: Ontological vs. Epistemic Distinction Restated
proposed.text: The Library 𝓜 is ontologically complete and may be infinite in cardinality. The coherence quotient 𝓜_C is the set of coherence-distinguishable equivalence classes. For any observer O, the accessible structure is 𝓜_C^O, a finite or bounded subset of the coherence quotient. Thus, while the Library is infinite, coherence makes it finite for any observer. This is the central insight of the NSFG singularity framework: singularities are coherence-based collapses of distinguishability, not cardinality-based infinities.
proposed.interpretation: The infinite Library is filtered by coherence equivalence, producing a finite accessible structure for any observer.

_revisions.rationale: Restates the central insight of the conversation as a formal conclusion.
